touches.text: Code that is no longer needed is deleted. Git history keeps it if we ever need it back.
It launches each device's cairn/devices/<device>/groundloop/pulse.py, each as its own process (5.8.3.4).

Watcher face: watches the code and the builders' work over time, reasons over it with graph trees (held by the librarian's delegation), and learns the failure modes. Learns from: code, chat logs, books, past projects, CC's failure modes.
Holds the charter tool's instance (17.6): build-quality feedback is hers.

It is the READY TO MERGE ONTO MAIN step of the pipeline: everything's proved, and merging implies pushing it up. With a branch per ticket (3.3.6), commits on the branch are as often as we like; the inspector is the step at ready to merge. Checking what a change touched belongs here; nothing hangs off the git post-commit hook.
charter: compiles a component's bounded state from its history. WHY: state is compiled from the component's tickets, never hand-edited (Law 5). Held by CodeMother.

What a gate asks is "does this meet the intentions", never who did it. Every intention carries a why, and so does every test case whose purpose is not plain. A change that makes a ticket or a test case meet the intentions better is good, and downstream supports it when the whys show it isn't a fast one. Measuring who did what serves none of that.
